directions.title: Science Bridge: The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis
directions.question: If the local control timescale varies smoothly in space, does anonymous organization change in a reproducible way?
directions.rationale: Literature mechanism: A spatially homogeneous state can become unstable and develop structure through reaction and transport, with small disturbances acting as triggers.  Translation warning: g001 is not Turing's multi-morphogen reaction-diffusion system. The experiment below is only a mechanism-inspired perturbation, not a reproduction of the paper.
directions.author: science-bridge:turing-1952-morphogenesis:10.1098/rstb.1952.0012
directions.strict_transfer_question: Without imposing a target geometry, do naturally occurring variations in local relaxation/transport timescale predict where anonymous organization appears?

directions.title: Science Bridge: Growth and division of active droplets provides a model for protocells
directions.question: Does a localized supply of field amplitude create a later growth-to-instability sequence rather than merely a larger static structure?
directions.rationale: Literature mechanism: A chemically driven material supply can make droplets grow until shape instabilities produce division-like daughter droplets.  Translation warning: A local energy pulse in g001 is not a chemically active droplet metabolism. It is an exploratory analogy used only to ask whether localized supply changes later instability.
directions.author: science-bridge:zwicker-2017-active-droplets:10.1038/nphys3984

source_reference.title: Growth and division of active droplets provides a model for protocells

directions.strict_transfer_question: In strict runs with no supplied target, do spontaneously growing localized structures show a size/growth threshold before independently defined instability or separation?

directions.title: Science Bridge: Kibble-Zurek mechanism and beyond in a holographic superfluid disk
directions.question: Do slower environmental changes alter defect and anonymous-transition statistics?
directions.rationale: Literature mechanism: Crossing a continuous transition at finite rate connects quench timescales to spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological-defect production.  Translation warning: Matching a quench-rate trend would not establish Kibble-Zurek universality in g001. The bridge only imports the falsifiable idea that transition rate may control defect statistics.
directions.author: science-bridge:kzm-2026-superfluid-disk:10.1038/s41467-026-69940-w
